runbooks.title: GPU Throttling: Thermal or Power-Limit Remediation
runbooks.scenario: GPU utilization is sustained above 90%, causing thermal throttling, reduced throughput, or node OOM events.
detection_signals: GPU utilization metric > 90% sustained for > 5 minutes
nvidia-smi reports thermal throttle (HW Slowdown = Active)

steps.detail: Run `kubectl get nodes -l workload=gpu -o wide` and check `nvidia-smi -q | grep 'Throttle Reasons'` on affected hosts. Note node IDs.
Run `kubectl drain <node-id> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` to evict workloads. Autoscaler will reschedule to healthy nodes.
Run `nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE` and compare against baseline in `/etc/nvidia/baseline_perf_profile.conf`. If diverged, restore defaults with `nvidia-smi -pm 1 && nvidia-smi -pl <baseline_watts>`.
Check datacenter DCIM dashboard for rack-level temperature. If ambient > 27°C, page Facilities team via `team-facilities-oncall@contoso-demo.invalid`.

steps.action: Reduce workload utilization cap if throttling persists
steps.detail: Update autoscaler policy: set `gpu_max_utilization_target` from 88% to 80% in ConfigMap `autoscaler-policy` in namespace `ai-factory`. Apply with `kubectl apply -f`.
Run `kubectl uncordon <node-id>` once GPU telemetry shows stable utilization < 85% for 10 consecutive minutes.
Update incident ticket with root cause (driver / thermal / workload), nodes affected, steps taken, and any policy changes. Notify team-nebula-oncall.

runbooks.escalation: If throttling affects > 4 nodes or cannot be resolved within 30 minutes, escalate to Priya Nanda (Platform Ops Lead) and Oscar Trent (Cloud Governance).

runbooks.title: Network Degradation: Elevated Latency or Packet Loss
runbooks.scenario: Sustained network latency spikes or packet loss (> 0.5%) observed between services or at external peering points.
detection_signals: Packet loss > 0.5% on any service-to-service path
BGP session flap alert from network monitoring

steps.detail: Run `mtr --report --report-cycles 60 <affected-endpoint>` from multiple source nodes to isolate whether degradation is at spine, leaf, or peering layer.
SSH to spine switch and run `show bgp summary` (Arista EOS) or equivalent. Confirm all BGP peers are Established. Log any flaps with timestamps.
Query change management system for any network changes in the last 2 hours. Correlate with anomaly start time. Check CE log for BGP or routing policy changes.
If primary path is degraded, update traffic policy to route through backup paths: `te-policy update --service nebula-inference --path backup`. Confirm with `te-policy status`.

steps.action: Isolate and roll back last network change
steps.detail: If a recent change correlates with the incident, initiate rollback via change management. Notify Marcus Chen (Network Engineering) immediately.
Confirm packet loss < 0.1% and p99 latency returns to within 20% of baseline for 15 consecutive minutes before declaring recovery.
Document root cause, timeline, customer impact, and remediation steps. Submit to Oscar Trent (Cloud Governance) within 48 hours of resolution.

runbooks.escalation: If packet loss > 2% or p99 latency > 500ms for > 15 minutes, escalate to Marcus Chen (Network Engineering) and page team-photon-oncall immediately.

runbooks.title: Cost Overrun: GPU Reserved Capacity Under-Utilization
runbooks.scenario: Reserved GPU instances are running at < 65% average utilization for > 2 consecutive days, generating cost anomalies vs budget.
detection_signals: Reserved instance utilization metric < 65% for > 48 hours
FinOps cost anomaly alert: reserved capacity idle hours > budget threshold
Training job queue depth near zero with reserved nodes idle
Cost dashboard shows daily GPU spend > 115% of budgeted rate

steps.detail: Query quota-manager API: `GET /v1/utilization/summary?window=48h&tier=reserved`. Confirm actual vs. target utilization. Check which services are underconsuming.
Review recent incidents (network, GPU, pipeline) that may have reduced job throughput. If jobs failed due to infra issues, utilization drop is a symptom, not root cause.
Update job-scheduler ConfigMap: set `backfill_enabled: true` and `backfill_priority: low`. Apply with `kubectl apply -f scheduler-config.yaml`. Lower-priority jobs will fill idle reserved capacity.
Check per-tenant quota allocations in quota-manager. If a tenant has reserved allocation but is not submitting jobs, reduce their reserved quota and return capacity to the shared pool.
If a job backlog exists, set scheduler priority to prioritize reserved-instance-eligible jobs: `scheduler-cli prioritize --tier reserved --window 24h`.
Send utilization recovery report to Sandra Voss (FinOps Director) including: root cause, actions taken, expected recovery timeline, and projected utilization for next 7 days.
Confirm cost anomaly webhook is active in Azure Monitor. If not, add alert rule: `reserved_utilization_pct < 65 for 24h → notify team-horizon-oncall`.

runbooks.escalation: If utilization remains < 60% after backfill is enabled for 24 hours, or if estimated weekly cost overrun exceeds $15,000, escalate to Sandra Voss (FinOps Director) and Oscar Trent (Cloud Governance).
